subproblem.title: Rescaled-secant limits lie in the range of the secant-approximating map
subproblem.statement:
Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P and x, w ∈ ℝ^P, and let A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map. Assume two things.
(Secant estimate) For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − x| < δ admits a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − x − Aa| ≤ ε|y − x|.
(Blow-up points) For every s > 0 there is λ₀ > 0 such that every λ ∈ (0, λ₀) admits y ∈ N with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.
Then w ∈ A(ℝ^d), i.e. w ∈ Set.range A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x w : Euclid P) (A : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P), (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y x < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - x - A a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - x‖) → (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∃ lam₀ : ℝ, 0 < lam₀ ∧ ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → lam < lam₀ → ∃ y ∈ N, ‖lam⁻¹ • (y - x) - w‖ < s) → w ∈ Set.range A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 2 and 7.
Notation. L := A(ℝ^d) = Set.range A.
1. L is closed. It is the range of the linear map A, a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, and finite-dimensional subspaces are closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). Hence it suffices to show w ∈ closure(L), i.e. that for every η > 0 there is ℓ ∈ L with |w − ℓ| < η.
2. Constants. Fix η > 0 and put s := η/2 > 0, K := |w| + s > 0 and ε := s/(K + 1) > 0. Then εK = sK/(K + 1) < s.
3. By the secant hypothesis for this ε, choose δ > 0 such that each y ∈ N with |y − x| < δ admits a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − x − Aa| ≤ ε|y − x|.
4. By the blow-up hypothesis for this s, choose λ₀ > 0 such that each λ ∈ (0, λ₀) admits y ∈ N with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.
5. Let λ := min(λ₀, δ/K)/2. Since λ₀ > 0 and δ/K > 0, we get λ > 0 and λ ≤ λ₀/2 < λ₀. Also λ ≤ (δ/K)/2 < δ/K, so λK < δ.
6. By step 4, take y ∈ N with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s. Then |λ⁻¹(y − x)| ≤ |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| + |w| < s + |w| = K. As λ > 0, |λ⁻¹(y − x)| = λ⁻¹|y − x|, so |y − x| < λK < δ.
7. By step 3 (y ∈ N and |y − x| < δ), take a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − x − Aa| ≤ ε|y − x|. Put ℓ := A(λ⁻¹a) ∈ L; by linearity ℓ = λ⁻¹Aa.
8. We have λ⁻¹(y − x) − ℓ = λ⁻¹(y − x − Aa). Hence |λ⁻¹(y − x) − ℓ| = λ⁻¹|y − x − Aa| ≤ λ⁻¹ε|y − x| < λ⁻¹ε(λK) = εK < s. This uses ε > 0, |y − x| < λK (step 6) and εK < s (step 2).
9. By the triangle inequality, |w − ℓ| ≤ |w − λ⁻¹(y − x)| + |λ⁻¹(y − x) − ℓ| < s + s = η.
10. As η > 0 was arbitrary, w ∈ closure(L) = L. So w = Ab for some b ∈ ℝ^d, i.e. w ∈ Set.range A.
proof_key_steps: L = A(ℝ^d) is a finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace, so it suffices to approximate w by points of L.
Given η > 0, set s = η/2, K = |w| + s and ε = s/(K + 1), so εK < s; take δ from the secant estimate and λ₀ from the blow-up hypothesis.
With λ = min(λ₀, δ/K)/2, a blow-up point y ∈ N satisfies |y − x| < λK < δ.
The secant estimate at y gives ℓ = A(λ⁻¹a) ∈ L with |w − ℓ| < s + εK < η; closedness of L gives w ∈ Set.range A.

audit.reason: Both approximation hypotheses and the continuous-linear-map range conclusion match exactly. The explicit positive constants and scale place the chosen point within the secant estimate, producing a range point within every prescribed tolerance. Finite-dimensional closedness completes the argument. No injectivity, x ∈ N, or nonzero-vector assumption is needed; zero-dimensional cases are covered.
